title: C# Questions & Answers - Attributes
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on attributes in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of the following generally does NOT inspect the attributes applied to code metadata?
questions.explanation: Compilers, the CLR, and runtimes like ASP.NET use attributes to change behavior or generate metadata. A standard linker primarily combines files and doesn't typically inspect custom attributes for logic.

questions.question: What is the correct way to apply an attribute to an entire Assembly?
questions.explanation: Global attributes (like assembly or module attributes) must be placed at the top of the file and use the 'assembly:' or 'module:' target specifier.

questions.question: Which method can be used to pass a specific parameter to an attribute property in C#?
questions.explanation: Attributes support both positional parameters (passed to the constructor by value) and named parameters (used to set specific properties or fields by name).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct form of applying an attribute in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, attributes are enclosed in square brackets []. The parenthesis are optional if there are no parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be a target for a custom attribute?
questions.explanation: Attributes can be applied to most programming elements (classes, methods, enums, etc.), but Namespaces are not valid targets for attributes in C#.

questions.question: Select the correct statement about Attributes used in C#.NET:

options.text: The CLR can change the behavior of the code depending on attributes applied to it
To receive three parameters, an attribute class must implement a zero-argument constructor
Custom attributes are created by deriving from System.ValueType

questions.explanation: The CLR and other tools use attributes (like [Serializable] or [SecurityAttribute]) to alter execution behavior. Custom attributes must be classes derived from 'System.Attribute'.

questions.question: What is the correct way to apply a custom attribute called 'Employer' which receives a name and an ID?

options.text: It can be applied to an assembly

questions.explanation: Attributes are versatile; they can be applied globally to an assembly or locally to classes, provided the AttributeUsage allows it.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common time to inspect an attribute in C#.NET?
questions.explanation: Attributes are primarily inspected at Runtime using Reflection to determine how the code should behave.

questions.question: To which elements can attributes be applied?
questions.explanation: Attributes are highly flexible and can be used to annotate methods, classes, properties, assemblies, and more.

questions.question: When is the [Serializable()] attribute typically inspected?
questions.explanation: The [Serializable] attribute is checked at runtime by serialization engines (like BinaryFormatter) to ensure the object is allowed to be serialized.
